Revise a plan's metadata without changing what it plans

Source: R/media-plan.R
revise.Rd

The metadata-only edit verb. Changes any of name, nickname, advertiser, planner, status, approved_on, objective, spend_basis and rationale, and leaves everything else — @data, @grain, @id, @parent_id, @subplans, @edits — exactly as it was. rationale is here because it describes the plan, not its spend: an author or a forecast can be added after the fact.

Usage

revise(plan, ...)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

...

Named metadata fields to change: name, nickname, advertiser, planner, status, approved_on (a Date or ISO string; only on an approved plan), objective, spend_basis (a correction, not a conversion), rationale (see build_scenario()). At least one.

Value

The same plan (same @id) with the named fields changed.

Details

spend_basis is here as a correction to a declaration, never a conversion. A plan imported as "media_net" whose figures were in fact client net is corrected with revise(spend_basis = "client_net"), and its numbers do not change. Turning media net into client net means applying a fee schedule, which is the caller's job.

Because @id is kept, the result is the same plan, revised, rather than a derivative of it; that is the difference from build_scenario(), which mints a new id and lineage.

This exists so that a consumer never has to rebuild a plan by naming its slots by hand — the habit that silently drops any slot added later. Use revise() for metadata, build_scenario() for spend, and attach_subplan() / detach_subplan() for structure.

Approval is set here: revise(status = "approved", approved_on = "2026-10-29"). The date is optional and never defaulted to today, and moving the status off "approved" clears it. There is no revision number to set: planners say Rev 3 meaning "the third approved version", which is a fact about the plan's lineage rather than the plan, so lineage() derives it, and current_approved() finds the latest.

Examples

p <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "Search"), planned_spend = c(80, 40)),
  grain = "channel", time = "week", name = "Q3 plan"
)
q <- revise(p, status = "approved", approved_on = "2026-10-29")
identical(q@id, p@id)
#> [1] TRUE
q@approved_on
#> [1] "2026-10-29"

# sending it back for review withdraws the approval and its date
revise(q, status = "to review")@approved_on
#> Date of length 0
